- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially in the first 5–7 days, then underestimates later days — adjust downward in early forecast windows.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70.0), model tends to overshoot and overcorrect — reduce forecast peak by 1–2% and smooth transition to next period.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance and fails to capture mean reversion — apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias to mid-to-late forecast window.
- Model underestimates downward trends after a spike — if last 3–5 days show decline, add 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment to forecast.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing true price momentum — shift forecast 1–2 days ahead for short-term spikes, but lag 1–2 days for long-term mean reversion.
